title: Delegated KMS patterns, RBAC v2 mappings, and SIEM-friendly audit exports
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is an operational reference for delegated key management models (customer BYOK and tenant-delegated patterns), the RBAC v2 role->action mapping we intend to adopt, and a canonical, SIEM-friendly audit log schema for key lifecycle and usage events. It focuses on the flows that matter for Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments and on the evidence automation needed for audits and incident investigations.

High-level models considered:
1) Customer-managed keys (BYOK) - customer owns CMKs in their KMS/HSM and Redwood is given limited access (unwrap/wrap) via a well-scoped service account or token. No raw key material leaves customer KMS.
2) Delegated Redwood-managed keys per-tenant - Redwood hosts CMKs but delegates operational controls (rotate/schedule) to tenant admins via RBAC policies and tenant-isolated key aliases.
3) Hybrid escrowed model (rare) - envelope keys held by Redwood with escrow via HSM-backed key vault; used only for regulated customers with explicit contracts.

Key lifecycle states (canonical): pending -> active -> scheduled_rotation -> disabled -> quarantined -> destroyed.
Important invariants: key metadata must include: owner_principal, tenancy_id, kms_provider, hsm_slot_id (if HSM), creation_source, last_rotation_id, rotation_policy_id, and attestation_status.

RBAC v2 role mappings (proposed):
- role:kms_admin: full lifecycle (create, update policy, schedule rotation, destroy, set-escrow). Bind to Redwood infra SAs and security ops.
- role:kms_operator: operational actions (rotate_now, bump-version, disable/enable). Bind to on-call SRE team and delegated support SAs after approval.
- role:key_owner: tenant-level admin who can schedule rotations, request export of public key material, and view audit/evidence. Bound to customer admin principals in BYOK and tenant admins in delegated model.
- role:key_decrypter (least privilege): decrypt/unwrap only. Bind to service identities that need data-plane access (e.g., model-serving processes).
- role:key_signer: sign-only for attestation/tamper-evidence.
- role:audit_viewer: read-only access to audit events and evidence blobs.

Mapping matrix (actions): create_key, create_key_version, schedule_rotation, rotate_now, disable_key, enable_key, destroy_key, rewrap_datakey, unwrap, wrap, get_public_key, attest_key, export_audit_evidence. Enforce via policy engine and tokens scoped to actions.

Rotation procedure (recommended automated flow):
1) Pre-rotation checks: ensure last successful backup of key metadata and evidence index exists; run inventory of active key versions and dependent services (via key-dependency index).
2) Create new key version (version N+1) in KMS/HSM with identical policy.
3) Rewrap data keys: best-effort rewrap at next use for streaming workloads; for bulk datasets, trigger rolling rewrap job with throughput caps.
4) Update aliases and discovery endpoints atomically (alias->new-version).
5) Emit rotation:event with rotation_plan_id and verification checklist attached.
6) Post-rotation validation: sample decrypts, integration smoke tests, and audit ingestion verification.
7) Schedule old-version archival and eventual destroy after retention window.

Emergency compromise steps (quick runbook):
- Immediately: disable affected key version, promote fallback key/alias, and create incident (jira:SEC-1289).
- Evidence: snapshot HSM audit log segment and create signed evidence blob, store in immutable object store with hash recorded in audit event.
- Notify customers and legal per SLA.
- Post-incident: rotate all affected keys, run full attestation, and produce an evidence package for compliance.

Audit log schema (canonical, SIEM-friendly): single-line JSON per event, minimal nesting, stable field names. Fields below are required for KMS events at Redwood: 
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- event_type (string) e.g., key.create, key.rotate, key.unwrap, key.disable, key.destroy, key.attest
- actor_id (string) canonical principal id (user:<email> | sa:<service-account>)
- actor_type (string) user|service|system|external
- principal_tags (list of strings) e.g., ["tenant:acme","env:prod"]
- tenant_id (string)
- key_id (string) global id for key alias
- key_version (string)
- action (string) low-level action e.g., unwrap, wrap, rewrap, rotate
- resource_path (string) e.g., /kms/keys/<id>/versions/<v>
- result (string) success|failure|partial
- failure_code (string) optional error code
- request_id (string) upstream request trace id
- src_ip (string) optional
- user_agent (string) optional
- correlation_id (string) for multi-step ops
- kms_provider (string) e.g., cloudkms:gcp, awskms, hsm:thales
- hsm_slot (string) when applicable
- evidence_blob_url (string) signed, immutable artifact (S3/GCS path)
- signature_valid (boolean as string) "true"|"false"
- raw_request_summary (string) sanitized summary for debug

Example event (single-line JSON to index in SIEM):
{"timestamp":"2025-02-28T18:44:12Z","event_id":"f3a9d6b2-2b6e-4a9d-9f1a-6f77c8b1eabc","event_type":"key.unwrap","actor_id":"sa:model-serving-42@redwood-internal","actor_type":"service","principal_tags":"tenant:acme,env:prod","tenant_id":"acme-prod-01","key_id":"km-7c9f2","key_version":"v12","action":"unwrap","resource_path":"/kms/keys/km-7c9f2/versions/v12","result":"success","request_id":"req-04e8f1","kms_provider":"hsm:vendor-A","hsm_slot":"slot-3","evidence_blob_url":"gs://redwood-evidence/km-7c9f2/v12/unwrap-req-04e8f1.tar.gz","signature_valid":"true"}

SIEM export patterns and suggestions:
- Index naming: redwood.kms.events.<region> with hot/infra retention tiers.
- Minimal pipeline: ingest -> parse JSON single-line -> enrich with tenant metadata -> index and route to long-term archive for events with evidence_blob_url.
- Detection rules (examples):
  * key-deletion: event_type == key.destroy AND result==success -> high severity if timestamp within last 24h for any core-tenant key.
  * excessive-unwraps: count(action==unwrap) by actor_id over 10m window > threshold -> alert and throttle.
  * out-of-band-rotation: rotation event where actor_type==user AND not scheduled -> investigate.
- Correlation: use correlation_id to tie rotate->rewrap->alias-change flows into one alertable incident.

Evidence automation and audit-pack generation:
- When rotation completes, pipeline automatically:
  1) collect rotation:event and all child unwrap/wrap events via correlation_id;
  2) bundle HSM audit segments, KMS audit records, and runbook snapshot;
  3) sign the bundle with root attestation key, store immutable object, and emit evidence_blob_url in a final rotation.complete event.
- Retention policy for evidence bundles: default 7 years for enterprise contracts, 1 year for standard.
- Attach evidence_blob_url to Jira incidents and keep the immutability hash pinned in the ticket.

Operational considerations and telemetry to build:
- Key-dependency index: map keys -> services -> config locations to allow pre-rotation impact analysis.
- Test harness: automated end-to-end tests that exercise unwrap/rewrap across providers (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Thales HSM).
- Cost/latency telemetry: track average unwrap latency per key_version and slap alerts when latency deviates >2x baseline after rotation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether evidence_blob_url should be stored in the tenant-visible audit console by default for BYOK customers (privacy/legal tradeoffs).
- Define precise retention SLAs per contract tier and embed them into rotation_policy metadata.
- Finalize RBAC role names and map to IAM primitives for GCP/AWS in infra playbook (action: infra/PR #78).

Next actions (owners):
- Marco: prototype SIEM ingestion pipeline for single-line JSON and populate sample index (due 2025-03-09).
- Li: implement key-dependency inventory job that tags keys with dependent services (due 2025-03-16).
- Sana: produce an attestation signer rotation plan and key ceremony checklist for HSM (due 2025-03-12).
- Priya (me): review and consolidate feedback into the final compliance runbook for the next audit window.

Notes / rough drafts style: contains checklist fragments, sample events, and runbook steps for engineers and auditors. This doc is intentionally conversational — will be formalized after team reviews.
